newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH DISMISS RAVANELLI TRANSFER RUMOURS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH DISMISS RAVANELLI TRANSFER RUMOURS.

text.p: English premier league club Middlesbrough stated emphatically on Wednesday Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli would not be signing for Manchester United.
Ravanelli sparked fevered transfer speculation on Tuesday when he broke off from training with the Italian squad in Florence and expressed an interest in playing for the English champions.
Wednesday's English newspapers claimed United were poised to make a 10 million pound ($15.7 million) bid for the 27-year-old, top scorer in the premier league this season.
United immediately dismissed the rumours as "absolute nonsense", and later on Wednesday Middlesbrough followed suit.
"Middlesbrough Football Club wish to make it clear that Fabrizio Ravanelli will not be joining Manchester United or any other club," chief executive Keith Lamb said.
"We have read and heard the stories, but there is absolutely no truth in them. We have had no contact with any club with regard to Ravanelli and we have no intention of selling him.
Ravanelli himself said he had been misrepresented in the English press.

"I never said Manchester United had made a bid," he told BBC Radio from Italy. "These stories just appeared in the newspapers and I don't know if they're true or not. If (United) do make a bid for me, they will do so to my club and not me."
He said he would happily extend his current four-year contract at the Teesside club for a further two years if Middlesbrough so wished.
